newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells 14.4 bln levs of 1-wk, 4-wk T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells 14.4 bln levs of 1-wk, 4-wk T-bills.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry on Tuesday sold two discount T-bill issues with maturities of one week and four weeks, yielding 3.56 percent and 17.34 percent respectively, the central bank said.
Bids were received for a total of 16.445 billion levs of paper but the ministry approved bids for 14.365 billion levs.
Bids received 9,477 million levs 6,968 million levs
Avg price of bids 96.51 pct 85.20 pct
Bids approved 8,007 million levs 6,358 million levs
Avg yield to maturity 3.56 pct 17.34 pct @
The ministry has offered the issues with no par value set in advance after it decided last week to issue short-term T-bills every day to regulate excessive banks' liquidity.

As a result of the ministry's decision the central bank suspended from Monday its daily open market operations through the revrepo facility with repurchase of up to two days, paving the way for the introduction of a tough fixed exchange rate regime.
Central bank open market operations would be curbed under a currency board system proposed by the International Monetary Fund to stabilise Bulgaria's crumbling financial sector. @
On Monday the ministry sold two issues of discount T-bill worth a total of 14.005 billion lev and with maturities of one week and four weeks, yielding 3.59 and 17.36 percent respectively.
